paragraphs: Let us put it to them: tell us about the report (khabar) on which a claim is to be founded — what is the source of its soundness, on the basis of what is it that we know it to be sound, and from where do we establish its truthfulness? If the opponent resorts to naẓar and istidlāl (rational reflection and demonstration) to authenticate the khabar, he has thereby annulled his own thesis that "a thing is known only by way of report" and has himself renounced it. If he claims, instead, that he knows the soundness and truth of the first report on the basis of another report, ask him about that second report: by what means do you establish its soundness and truthfulness? And he will be forced to the same argument to which he was forced regarding the first report — and so on, ad infinitum.

It should be said to him: if your thesis is sound, no report can ever be confirmed, and no knowledge can be gained via reports at all.[{2}] For if every report can be confirmed only by another, then no report can ever be confirmed — in the same way that the testimony of two witnesses is not confirmed unless they are individuals whose testimony is legally admissible, and the legal admissibility of their testimony can in turn be confirmed only by yet other witnesses.[{3}]

The same holds [in the legal case]: and so the testimony of one pair of witnesses is not validated except by another pair, and there is no terminus to this; therefore it is impossible for Zayd's claim against ʿAmr regarding a financial matter to be validated at all on these terms.[{5}]

Are not reports of two kinds — some true and some false? When they grant this (as they must, since it is their own position), say to them: tell us, then, about the means of distinguishing a sound report (al-khabar al-ṣaḥīḥ) from a defective report (al-khabar al-saqīm) — is the distinction made by report, or by naẓar?[{6}] If they answer "by naẓar," they have annulled their thesis and have confirmed naẓar. If they answer "by [another] report," ask them about that second report: by what means do you distinguish it from a defective report? They are forced to exactly the same consequence we forced upon them in the previous step.

They should also be asked about the prophetic messenger:[{7}] by what means is he distinguished from those who lie? If they answer "by the appearance of miracles (al-muʿjizāt)," say: then you have made knowledge obligatory by something other than report. Moreover — let it be said to them: what would your view be if someone said the reverse, namely that the one who does not work miracles is the truthful one, and the one who does work miracles is the liar? Is it possible to falsify that claim by anything other than al-maʿqūl — the rational faculty — as opposed to report? In this lies the abolition of their thesis, and the confirmation of the probative force of al-ʿaql (ḥujjat al-ʿaql).[{8}] ---
